chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Uthman ibn Isa from al-Ala' ibn al-Fadl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: Honor is the garment of God and Pride is His lower garment, so whoever takes anything from them, God will cast him into Hell.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Honor is God's garment and Pride is His lower garment?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* establishes a theological distinction between divine majesty and human pride, identifying 'Al-Izz' and 'Al-Kibr' as exclusive attributes of Allah. It warns that usurping these divine qualities leads to spiritual downfall, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegesis where 'Kibr' is often linked to the arrogance of Iblis. The narration serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate humility by recognizing that true honor is a gift from God, not an inherent human right.
